abstract.p: Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs) demonstrate strong capabilities in visual understanding and description, yet often suffer from hallucinations-attributing incorrect or misleading features to images. We observe that LVLMs disproportionately focus on a small subset of image tokens-termed blind tokenswhich are typically irrelevant to the query (e.g., background or non-object regions). We hypothesize that such attention misalignment plays a key role in generating hallucinated responses. To mitigate this issue, we propose Attentional Vision Calibration (AVISC), a test-time approach that dynamically recalibrates the influence of blind tokens without modifying the underlying attention mechanism. AVISC first identifies blind tokens by analyzing layer-wise attention distributions over image tokens, then employs a contrastive decoding strategy to balance the influence of original and blind-tokenbiased logits. Experiments on standard benchmarks, including POPE, MME, and AMBER, demonstrate that AVISC effectively reduces hallucinations in LVLMs.
